verdict.rationale: Reader turns any URL into LLM-friendly output via a simple prefix (r.jina.ai), and the docs explicitly position it as clean, LLM-ready text for complex or dynamic pages. Each part of the story is covered: rendering through a headless-Chrome engine and wait-for-selector, blocking through a hosted rotating proxy pool that handles anti-bot challenges (API key required), and output formats such as Markdown with frontmatter and semantic chunking. The community items only raise an open question about JS support and show that an API key is required, so they do not contradict the capability. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of output cleanliness and anti-bot success on real-world pages.
